lab.title: Lab
lab.intro: A space for my experiments and notes at the intersection of technology and cultural heritage — from image enhancement and computer vision to ideas on digital museums and heritage digitization. Updated over time.

demos.title: Low-light image enhancement
demos.summary: Grayscale conversion, histogram equalization, CLAHE and gamma correction, with before/after side by side and a histogram.
demos.explain: This demo mirrors my computer vision work on night-vision image enhancement. It reads pixels from a canvas in the browser and applies grayscale conversion, gamma correction, histogram equalization and a CLAHE-lite — per-tile histograms, a clip limit, then bilinear interpolation between neighbouring tile lookup tables — to a procedurally generated dark test image (or a picture you upload), showing before and after side by side with their luminance histograms. Gamma, clip limit and tile grid are adjustable with sliders, and the code itself is editable.

demos.title: Editable 3×3 convolution kernel
demos.summary: Presets for Sobel, sharpen, box blur and emboss — edit the nine numbers and watch the output update live.
demos.explain: Convolution kernels are the basic building block of image processing: every output pixel is a weighted sum of its 3×3 neighbourhood. This demo ships presets for Sobel X / Y / magnitude, sharpen, box blur and emboss, and you can edit the nine numbers and the divisor directly — the output image updates live.

demos.title: Pathfinding visualizer
demos.summary: Draw walls and compare eight pathfinding algorithms, or race up to four of them on the same map.
demos.explain: Draw walls, drag the start and goal, and run BFS, greedy best-first, Dijkstra, A*, bidirectional A*, jump point search, Theta* or D* Lite. The heuristic switches between Manhattan, octile and Euclidean, and diagonal steps can be turned on. Compare mode runs two to four algorithms on the same map and outlines whoever visits the fewest cells. With D* Lite you can add a wall during the run: that cell flashes and the route is repaired incrementally. The table lists cells visited, path length and time, and whether the result is optimal for the current settings.

lab.network: The interactive demo runs in a sandboxed iframe; its bundler is loaded from CodeSandbox.

about.title: About me
paragraphs: I'm Westly Tan Xue Le (陈学礼), based in Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia.

From 2015 to 2020, I completed my Bachelor's and Master's in Computer Science at St. John's University in Taiwan. During those years I took part in national-level projects and was involved in early AI development, where I was responsible for computer vision algorithms — for example, using grayscale operations to enhance night-vision imagery. The low-light enhancement methods I used include grayscale conversion, histogram equalization (including CLAHE), gamma correction and denoising.

From 2021 to 2024, I turned to the humanities and earned an academic Master's in Archaeology at Zhengzhou University in China. In 2024 I interned at the Henan Museum, providing direction and technology for its digital museum — putting my technical background to work in cultural heritage.

In 2025 I joined Stayrene as IT Lead and was promoted to IT Manager in 2026. I currently lead a team of 2 and am responsible for the company's internal business systems, including cleaning operations, finance, UMS/PMS, an owner portal and ticketing.

Computer science and archaeology are an unusual pairing, but to me both are about seeing clearly — one helps machines see images, the other helps people see history. I'm looking to keep growing in technology leadership and in work where technology meets cultural heritage.
